title: COIN: Uncertainty-Guarding Selective Question Answering for Foundation Models with Provable Risk Guarantees
research_question: Can a foundation-model question-answering system calibrate an uncertainty threshold that gives a high-probability bound on conditional answer failure while retaining substantially more correct answers than existing conformal-alignment selection methods?
methodology: COIN first evaluates answer failures and uncertainty scores on a held-out calibration set, computes an upper confidence bound on the conditional failure rate for candidate uncertainty thresholds, and selects the largest threshold satisfying a user-specified risk requirement. The default variant uses a one-sided Clopper-Pearson bound, while another variant uses a Hoeffding bound. The threshold is fixed before deployment so test-time selection only compares each answer's uncertainty with the calibrated threshold. Experiments cover CommonsenseQA, TriviaQA, and the multimodal MMVet benchmark across multiple language and vision-language models and several uncertainty estimators.

key_findings.finding: Across the reported repeated trials, both the Clopper-Pearson and Hoeffding COIN variants kept mean empirical conditional failure rates below the user-specified target risk levels for the evaluated foundation models.

COIN retained substantially more admissible answers than conformal alignment in several settings; for Qwen2.5-14B on CommonsenseQA, the Clopper-Pearson variant reached power 0.85 at target risk 0.15, reported as 0.36 higher than conformal alignment.
On TriviaQA, the reported power advantage over conformal alignment reached about 0.4 in some evaluated risk settings.
The method continued to satisfy the evaluated risk targets when only one tenth of the available examples were allocated to calibration in the reported limited-calibration experiment.

Because the threshold is pre-calibrated, COIN's deployment-time decision is a threshold comparison rather than a test-time comparison against every calibration example as required by the conformal-alignment baseline.
Alternative uncertainty estimators can be substituted into the framework, and some produced greater selection power while maintaining the empirical risk constraint.

limitations: The statistical guarantee assumes calibration and future examples are independently and identically distributed from the same underlying distribution, so it does not directly guarantee control under non-stationary temporal drift.
The calibrated threshold is static rather than continually updated online as the stream distribution evolves.

For open-ended answers, correctness is converted into a binary admission decision by a chosen evaluator such as semantic similarity, entailment, or an LLM judge, so the guarantee is relative to that evaluator rather than to factual truth in an unrestricted sense.
The experiments cover three QA benchmarks and a finite collection of models rather than arbitrary long-form multi-source generation.
The controlled quantity is an aggregate conditional failure rate for retained answers, not evidence completeness within compound claims or attribution of individual subclaims to source evidence.
The method does not model longitudinal omission of due, resolved, or superseded work-item states.
No public code release was identified in the paper text that was read.
raw_claims: COIN selects answers whose uncertainty is no greater than a calibration-derived threshold.
The target quantity is the conditional failure rate among answers that the system chooses to retain.
The method constructs a high-probability upper bound on this conditional failure rate during calibration.
The default implementation uses an exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson bound.
A Hoeffding-based version is also evaluated.
Experiments include CommonsenseQA, TriviaQA, and MMVet.
Power is defined as the proportion of admissible answers that the selection procedure retains.
The method is evaluated over repeated calibration and test trials.
The formal risk argument assumes independent and identically distributed samples.
